messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: P1 - gpu-pool-us-west-2 degraded (elevated 5xx/429, node flapping). Pager routed to primary on-call neha.

neha: saw the page, I'm on it. quick summary: autoscaler is healthy but 3/20 nodes in the main GPU pool are cycling with OOM-like crashes and kernel errors; traffic spikes to embedding endpoints are amplifying tail latency.

derek: assigning myself as secondary for the next hour. will grab logs + start isolating nodes.

neha: thanks. immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert a subset of traffic to fallback pool (cpu-backed or smaller model) 2) drain and cordon the 3 flapping nodes 3) trigger a temporary scale-up of dedicated fallback fleet 4) enable KV cache conservative mode to reduce mem usage.

ash: re-routing rule is ready. sending canary 5% to fallback pool now. /deploy-route canary --service=embeddings --to=fall-back-5pct

deploy-bot: deploy started: route canary 5% -> embeddings-fallback (job id: dpl-2026-03-14-0918).

neha: adding commands and logs I'm using:
```
# check OOM / kernel errors
journalctl -u docker --since "15 minutes ago" | grep -E "OOM|killed|kswapd"
# cordon and drain node
kubectl cordon gpu-node-47 && kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# throttle cache
curl -XPOST "https://ops-api/redwood/v1/config/cache_mode" -d '{"mode":"conservative"}'
```

amina: I've alerted CS & triage. putting a note into the incident channel for any customers hitting 429s. support-bot will start collecting logs from affected orgs.

support-bot: collecting logs for customers: acme-inc, betaai, druidlabs. will attach request_ids 0-4 to the ticket.

neha: current metrics: p95 gen latency up from 120ms -> 620ms, 5xx rate up to 2.3% (baseline 0.02%), some 429 spikes on embeddings at 10:05:00 UTC. No full region outage. Impact: degraded performance and increased latency; small number of requests receiving 429.

derek: I've cordoned gpu-node-47 and gpu-node-53. both show repeated nv_peer_mem / driver faults in dmesg. draining started. I'll isolate any instance-level sidecars to reduce noise.

neha: scaling fallback pool by +8 (spin up smaller gpus / ampere-t4-equivalent) to handle routing. scale request submitted: infra-autoscale --pool embeddings-fallback --add=8 --priority=high

deploy-bot: scale job queued id: scale-2026-03-14-0922. estimated warmup ~5min.

amina: CS update posted: "We're investigating elevated latency and intermittent 429s on embeddings. Mitigations in progress; limited customer impact. We'll update in 30 minutes or earlier." :wave:

ash: can we reduce batch size on embeddings temporarily? there's a flag in model config. small change, should reduce memory per-request.

neha: yes. applying conservative batch sizes. patch:
```
PATCH /configs/models/embeddings/serve
{"batch_max_tokens": 512, "batch_max_requests": 8}
```

neha: progress update — canary at 5% shows latency on fallback pool at p95 ~200ms, reduced 429s for canary traffic. production 429s dropping slowly.

derek: nodes GPU47/53 show kernel GPU reset events around 09:03 — looks like a driver bug surfaced under memory pressure. I'll escalate to infra and add to postmortem.

amina: action item for CS: prepare outbound note if we need to call customers. tagging @cs-leads.

neha: immediate next steps for current shift: 1) keep canary at 5% for 15min, then ramp to 20% if stable 2) finish draining the two flappers, cordon them 3) watch autoscaler and prepare rollback plan if fallback becomes overloaded 4) collect full dmesg + nvidia-smi history and attach to incident.

neha: who owns the follow-up postmortem once this is resolved? I'm on primary for the next 90m, but would prefer derek to run the postmortem since he has node-level logs.

derek: I will own the postmortem. I'll create the PM doc and link runbook sections for driver/kernel OOM handling.

neha: handoff for next on-call (in 1h): primary -> amina, secondary -> derek. coverage notes: amina to monitor canary ramp and customer comms; derek to finalize node forensics.

amina: acknowledged. will be primary at 10:22 UTC. I'll keep the canary slow and open a follow-up thread if p95 > 400ms.

neha: runbook pointers: /runbooks/gpu-node-failure, /runbooks/embeddings-fallback, /runbooks/customer-impact-template. also added a short checklist in the incident doc: cordon, drain, scale fallback, reduce batch, collect dmesg, escalate driver.

derek: collecting artifacts now. attaching commands:
```
# nvidia-smi loop dump
for i in {1..30}; do nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,memory.used --format=csv >> /tmp/gpu-dump-$HOSTNAME.csv; sleep 5; done
# driver version & kernel logs
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
```

neha: status at 09:55 UTC: canary 5% healthy, 429 rate dropping to 0.4%, p95 260ms. keeping actions open until nodes fully drained and fallback warmed to target capacity.

amina: I'll post a short SLO-facing blurb at 10:00 and ping cs-leads.

neha: final notes for handoff: open tasks (strings): [drain node-53, confirm fw & driver versions, complete postmortem, reconcile billing from fallback scale, follow up with infra team on possible driver regression].

neha: leaving the bridge for next shift; tagging @amina and @derek again. thanks all. :heart:

support-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-0314-1810. linked customers: acme-inc, betaai, druidlabs.

IncidentBot: Incident P1 status updated -> mitigated (partial). next update scheduled 30min.

amina: taking over as primary. will keep monitoring and will escalate if we see regression.

(End of thread)
